claims.text: AC-STEM can investigate the thermal behavior of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles at atomic-scale resolution.
AC-STEM can provide insight into the structural properties of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
AC-STEM observations can provide insight into thermodynamic contributions to the nanoparticle structure.
The initial nanoparticles are nearly equiatomic nanoalloys containing Au, Co, Cu, Ni, and Pt.
Exposure to high temperatures can induce structural changes in AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Thermally induced structural changes can be visualized directly at the atomic scale using AC-STEM.
The thermal stability of the nanoparticles is presently based on theoretical speculation.
The investigation is limited by the availability of experimental data and the accuracy of AC-STEM measurements.
In situ AC-STEM at varying temperatures can measure atomic structure and thermal stability.
Failure to observe thermally induced structural changes would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis primarily claims that AC-STEM can investigate thermal behavior, but the falsification rule treats absence of structural change as falsification. Observing no change could instead be a valid AC-STEM result demonstrating thermal stability, so it would not by itself falsify the method's investigative capability.
